title: ✨ Magic & the Cosmos
rawNotionMarkup: This page records Eryndor's underlying magical principles, the natural satellite system, recognised disciplines, Khazari traditions, everyday magic and the lost ancient art of Natural Magic harmonisation. The rules below apply across the world; individual cultures and schools interpret and practise them differently. ## Three foundations of magic Eryndor's magic has three interconnected foundations: 1. Natural Magic, the energy generated by Eryndor itself and present throughout the world. 2. Lunar influences, the individual magical disciplines strengthened by the moons as their orbital positions change. 3. Magical compatibility, the inherent affinities and resistances between different disciplines. These foundations interact, but none replaces the others. Natural Magic exists even when a moon's influence is weak. Disciplines have compatibility whether or not their moons are aligned. A strong lunar condition does not grant a novice mastery. ## Natural Magic — the World's Breath Eryndor itself produces magic. Older Khazari writings call this planetary magic the World's Breath; “Natural Magic” is the broadly used working name. Natural Magic permeates the world: - Stone, mountains and underground formations. - Rivers, lakes, oceans and groundwater. - Plants, forests and living creatures. - Atmosphere and natural phenomena. - The wider environment and the systems that sustain life. It is the underlying magical energy of an inherently magical planet. Everyone interacts with Natural Magic to some degree, although awareness, aptitude and control vary greatly. Ordinary people may draw on it instinctively or indirectly through work and surroundings. Trained practitioners can learn to sense, channel and shape it deliberately. It is not exclusive to a particular people, class or profession. Natural Magic remains present even when lunar influences are weak. Magic never disappears simply because a moon is elsewhere in its orbit. Its presence does not automatically make everyone a capable spellcaster, and it does not remove the need for training, judgement, materials, preparation, concentration or skill. ## Eryndor's moons and rings ### Established satellite structure Eryndor has approximately 26–30 natural satellites: - Four major moons. - Seven medium moons. - Ten small moons. - Five to nine tiny captured bodies. The exact total is not fixed beyond this approximate range. Ilyra, the larger of the two originally established moons, and Vaelis, the smaller, remain part of the system. Their identities are not retconned. ### The planetary rings Eryndor has a vast, irregular planetary ring system formed from debris left by ancient lunar destruction. Several moons collided in the distant past. Some shattered; later collisions produced further fragments, and some debris settled into stable orbits. The rings contain countless fragments and occasional larger bodies. Meteor showers and occasional atmospheric debris falls form part of Eryndor's natural history. The modern satellite system is broadly stable but gravitationally complex and continually changing. The full ancient sequence of collisions and the exact present orbits are not completely understood. The ancient lunar cataclysms also fundamentally changed Eryndor's magical environment; their full chronology, causes and magical consequences remain incompletely understood by modern peoples. ### What remains unknown The exact roster of moon names, sizes, orbital periods, trajectories, individual magical disciplines and long-term cycles remains to be developed. Do not invent a complete roster, orbital table or list of magical domains without deliberately establishing it as new canon. ## Lunar Magic — each moon governs a discipline Every moon individually governs a magical discipline and continuously strengthens users and workings of that discipline throughout Eryndor. - A moon's orbital position determines the strength of its influence at a given time. - Its phase alone is not the determining factor. - The relative positions and relationships between moons affect the strength of their respective influences. - Alignments may amplify multiple disciplines simultaneously. - Different orbital configurations can change magical conditions over days, seasons, years and much longer cycles. - Unusual proximity can produce interference, resonance or instability. The complete moon-to-discipline roster has not yet been developed. Do not assume Ilyra or Vaelis governs a particular named discipline unless that assignment is established later. ## Magical compatibility Disciplines have inherent affinities and degrees of compatibility. Some cooperate naturally, some require considerable skill to combine, and some resist or interfere with one another. Compatibility exists independently of lunar proximity. Aligned moons are not required for two disciplines to interact. Lunar conditions may strengthen or complicate an interaction, but they do not create its underlying compatibility. Illustrative affinities include: - Runecraft + Deepcraft: Structural and magical reinforcement. - Healing + Natural Magic: Restoration. - Elemental Magic + Nature Magic: Environmental workings. - Illusion + Divination: Perception and revelation. - Runecraft + protective or binding magic: Barriers and bindings. These examples are not a complete or universally fixed compatibility chart. The exact degree of compatibility, practical methods and risks depend on the disciplines, practitioner, working and conditions. ## Lunar imbalance and catastrophic risk When moons approach one another unusually closely, their magical influences can interfere, resonate or become unstable. Possible consequences include: - Excessive amplification or uncontrolled surges. - Unexpected interaction between disciplines. - Unstable enchantments and ancient mechanisms. - Disturbances in magical barriers or containment systems. - Changes in magical creatures and environmental conditions. - Regional or wider magical disruptions. An actual collision could produce a catastrophic magical imbalance. The destruction could release enormous magical energy and alter Eryndor's magical environment for centuries or millennia. It may also create new fragments, smaller moons and further orbital disturbances. These are possible consequences, not a guarantee that every close approach or collision produces an identical outcome. Lunar influence affects the whole world, not only spellcasters: magical creatures, enchanted objects, ancient structures, barriers and the natural environment may also be affected. Exceptional celestial conditions do not grant mastery automatically. A novice remains a novice; knowledge, training, aptitude, judgement and circumstances determine what can be achieved. ## The lost ancient art of Natural Magic harmonisation In ancient times, practitioners from several civilisations discovered sophisticated ways to harness and refine Natural Magic as a common medium between magical disciplines. This method did more than draw additional energy from the planet. Practitioners used Natural Magic as an intermediary to: - Strengthen magical workings. - Reduce resistance between disciplines. - Harmonise combinations that would otherwise be difficult. - Connect disciplines beyond their ordinary affinities. - Harmonise multiple lunar influences. - Create unified magical workings with greater efficiency than modern practitioners generally achieve. ### True fusion versus combined spellcasting True fusion is distinct from merely casting two spells together or using one discipline to support another. It creates a unified working from multiple disciplines, with Natural Magic serving as the common intermediary. The method did not eliminate the need for understanding, skill, control or judgement. It was a sophisticated technique, not a shortcut that allowed untrained people to combine any magic safely. ### Loss and possible survival Knowledge of the method was lost for unknown reasons. Possible explanations include civilisational collapse, catastrophe, deliberate suppression, destroyed infrastructure or incomplete fragments surviving without the original principles. None is established as the truth. Surviving traces may include ruins, manuscripts, instruments, incomplete teachings and oral traditions. ### Origins are not exclusively Khazari The method predates the First Throne and is not exclusively Khazari, dwarven or First Throne knowledge. Its first practitioners may have lived on any of Eryndor's five continents. Knowledge could have spread by trade, migration, conquest, exploration or cultural exchange; different civilisations may also have developed independent approaches. The most complete surviving knowledge may exist far from Avarra. Do not assume every relevant ruin or fragment on Avarra is connected to the First Throne. Gloin's hypothesis that Common or Natural Magic might act as an intermediary between specialised disciplines remains a developing personal hypothesis. He has not discovered the ancient method, its precise operation or its complete history. Elska's discreet research into historical attempts to use ambient or Common Magic as an intermediary is a separate research task; do not involve Hadrik in it without Gloin's choice. ## Recognised broad magical disciplines The setting already recognises broad disciplines including: - Arcana. - Nature. - Divination. - Bloodcraft. - Runecraft. - Shadowcraft. These are broad categories, not an exhaustive list of every discipline governed by every moon. The lunar roster remains unfinished. ## Khazari magical traditions Khazari practice includes specialised traditions. They are learnable through aptitude, training and work; they are not exclusive to nobility. 1. Runecraft: Symbols direct energy into objects and structures. It is used to enchant weapons, armour, buildings and mechanisms. 2. Deepcraft: Work with stone, earth and underground structures. Practitioners may sense weaknesses, water and subtle changes in rock, and manipulate small amounts of stone. 3. Forgebinding: Enchantment integrated with craftsmanship, producing durable weapons, self-maintaining edges and other crafted effects. 4. Hearthmagic: Warmth, preservation, protection and household or settlement workings. 5. Stonecalling: A rare tradition of communication or sensing with a mountain, including sensing movement through rock. Its limits and full practice remain to be developed. 6. Ancestral Binding: Controversial workings linked to bloodlines, oaths and hereditary obligations. The First Throne mastered this discipline. These traditions should not be treated as the only magic practised by Khazari, nor as the universal model for every other people. ## First Throne script and runic principles First Throne script is instruction-based. A symbol's meaning depends on its arrangement and context; the same symbol can function differently in another sequence. Three introductory symbols currently established in Gloin's study are: - Hold: Maintain a state or position. - Within: Define a boundary or enclosed space. - Until Command: A condition remains active until an authorised instruction is received. Together, an arrangement might express: “Maintain the enclosed state until an authorised command is received.” This does not prove that the command releases the enclosure; it might release, reinforce or change the system. Interpretation requires context, full sequence and technical understanding. ## Everyday and practical magic Magic is not confined to elite scholars, legendary heroes, royal courts or dangerous ancient mechanisms. It can have ordinary uses throughout Eryndor in farming, medicine, construction, transport, military service, crafts and household life. Examples of modest, specialised workings may include: - Preserving food or helping keep stores dry. - Warming a room or improving a lamp. - Detecting damp, disease or structural weakness. - Encouraging healthy soil or protecting crops. - Keeping tools in good condition. - Stabilising a wound or supporting medical care. - Purifying a small amount of water. - Reinforcing a shield or supporting field repairs. ### Practical limitations and access - A simple charm is not a substitute for every skill, tool or medical treatment. - A person may know a little practical magic without being a professional mage. - Some people use prepared charms or enchanted tools without being able to cast or fully understand the working. - Access varies with local culture, resources, cost, education, practitioners, laws, guilds and the strength of effect required. - A village healer may know a few useful workings; a wealthy city may support specialists, workshops and regulated magical services. - Magical aptitude is not the same as practical knowledge. Someone with little innate talent may learn simple procedures, while a naturally gifted person may lack the training to use that talent safely. - Magic can require time, concentration, materials, preparation, maintenance and recovery. It should not erase scarcity, expertise, injury, disease, labour or sound judgement. - Different peoples and regions develop their own ordinary magical practices. Khazari runic craft is one tradition, not the universal model. - Military magic may support signals, field repairs, protective work, medical care, detection and engineering, without turning every soldier into a battle-mage. Specific everyday spells, charms, tools, costs, regulations and regional customs will be developed as they become relevant. Their prevalence and sophistication vary across communities. ### Magic's effect on technological development Magic is one of the reasons Eryndor follows a different technological path from our own world. Practical workings and enchanted craft can fulfil some functions that might otherwise encourage the development of electrical systems, modern communications, industrial automation or other technologies. This changes the incentives and economic pressures that drive invention. Magic does not replace all engineering. Mechanical systems remain valuable where they are more reliable, scalable, economical or easier to maintain. Magitech combines physical engineering with runic or magical components, but still requires skilled labour, materials, maintenance and access to practitioners. This contributes to Eryndor's established technological boundary: high-medieval daily life, sophisticated regional engineering, and selected steam, hydraulic and magitech systems, without an automatic progression into modern or fully Victorian industrial society. This is a different path of development, not a world where invention has stopped. The detailed technological framework is recorded on the Technology, Craft & Infrastructure page. ## Magic canon boundaries - Natural Magic is always present; weak lunar influence does not mean magic vanishes. - Lunar orbital position, not phase alone, determines the strength of a moon's influence. - Each moon governs an individual discipline, but the complete roster remains open. - Compatibility exists independently of lunar alignment. - The lost Natural Magic harmonisation method is distinct from ordinary reinforcement or simultaneous spellcasting. - The lost method's origins, exact operation, surviving locations and reason for disappearance are unknown. - Gloin's theory remains his own developing hypothesis, not a confirmed rediscovery. - No new spell, discipline, moon-domain assignment, magical law or ancient technique becomes established simply because it would be convenient. Record new developments deliberately and with their evidence status.
